plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to shading my bid - it only risks losing profitable auctions or overpaying isn't a concern since payment is based on the second-highest bid. With my value at $46, I should bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than others, paying only what's necessary.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to shading my bid below value—it only risks losing profitable wins. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so, and I never overpay since the price is set by the second-highest bid. With no repeated rounds to exploit, truthful bidding is optimal here.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it doesn't matter what others bid, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losing money. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $28 to maximize expected profit.
